docs.title: always_relevant
docs.text:
The empty <always_relevant/> child marks its parent question as relevant across topic changes.

<parameters question_type="wh_question" predicate="word_meaning">
  <always_relevant/>
</parameters>

It has no attributes and is used inside a question's parameters. Use it when a question should remain available as relevant even when the dialogue appears to have changed topic. This setting is separate from explicit question dependencies; see Default questions and dependencies.

docs.title: Ask features
docs.text:
An <ask_feature> declares a feature predicate to ask about while narrowing an incremental-search question.

<parameters question_type="wh_question" predicate="contact"
            source="service" incremental="true">
  <service_query type="wh_question" predicate="available_contact"/>
  <ask_feature predicate="contact_name"/>
  <ask_feature predicate="contact_city" kpq="true"/>
</parameters>
Attribute Meaning predicate Required feature predicate associated with the searched entity. kpq Optional Boolean. When true, asks whether the user knows the feature value.

The parent question's feature predicates are used to refine the result set; they must be declared in the ontology and associated with the parent predicate via feature_of. Ask features are relevant when question parameters have incremental="true". A service-sourced search also requires a service_query.

docs.title: Default questions
docs.text:
Each top-level <default_question> declares a question treated as a default question in the domain. It uses the shared question syntax:

<default_question type="wh_question" predicate="destination"/>

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
A <dependency> associates a dependent question with one question it depends on. Tala uses the relationship when assessing question relevance.

<dependency type="wh_question" predicate="room_date">
  <question type="wh_question" predicate="room_type"/>
</dependency>

The dependency's type/predicate identify the dependent question; each child question identifies the one question it depends on. See Question parameters for always_relevant, which controls relevance independently.

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
A goal declares an action for the system to perform or a question for it to resolve. Goals are the units that plans fulfill.

<goal type="perform" action="book_room">
  <plan>
    <findout type="wh_question" predicate="room_date"/>
    <invoke_service_action name="BookRoom"/>
  </plan>
</goal>
Attribute Use type Required by the Tala compiler: perform or resolve. action Ontology action for a perform goal. question_type Resolve-goal question type; defaults to wh_question. predicate Predicate used by a predicate-backed resolve question. accommodate_without_feedback Suppresses accommodation feedback. reraise_on_resume Controls feedback when a goal resumes. restart_on_completion Restarts the goal after completion. max_answers Maximum answers returned for a user question. alternatives_predicate Distinguishes alternatives when multiple answers are allowed.

Predicate-backed resolve yes/no goal:

<goal type="resolve" question_type="yn_question" predicate="need_visa"/>

Write predicate as an attribute on <goal>, as shown. A direct <proposition> child of <goal> does not accept a value attribute.

Other children include plan, postplan, downdate_condition, preferred, and superaction.

  • <preferred/> marks a goal as preferred unconditionally. A preferred proposition makes it preferred when that fact is present.
  • <superaction name="…"/> associates the goal's action with a broader ontology action that it can satisfy.
  • postcond remains in the XSD, but the compiler does not process it. Use explicit downdate_condition children instead.

For example, mark booking a room as a preferred way to arrange travel when the user has selected business class:

<goal type="perform" action="book_room">
  <preferred>
    <proposition predicate="travel_mode" value="business_class"/>
  </preferred>
  <superaction name="arrange_travel"/>
  <plan><invoke_service_action name="BookRoom"/></plan>
</goal>

See Plans and postplans, Plan items, and Downdate conditions.

docs.title: Question hints
docs.text:
A <hint> supplies information after the user negatively accepts a question (for example, “I don't know”), before the question is asked again.

<parameters question_type="yn_question" predicate="added_water">
  <hint>
    <inform insist="true">
      <proposition predicate="helpful_information" value="added_water_hint"/>
    </inform>
  </hint>
</parameters>

The XML schema requires exactly one inform child. Define multiple hint elements to present hints in order; after the final hint, it is repeated until the question is answered. Hints are children of a question's parameters.

For example, two ordered hints for a WH question:

<parameters question_type="wh_question" predicate="ingredient_quantity">
  <hint><inform insist="true"><proposition predicate="helpful_information" value="quantity_hint_1"/></inform></hint>
  <hint><inform insist="true"><proposition predicate="helpful_information" value="quantity_hint_2"/></inform></hint>
</parameters>

docs.title: Iterators
docs.text:
An <iterator> names a sequence of propositions that a plan can consume one at a time.

<iterator name="room_iterator">
  <enumerate randomize="false" limit="5">
    <proposition predicate="room_type" value="single"/>
    <proposition predicate="room_type" value="double"/>
  </enumerate>
</iterator>

name is required. Exactly one enumerate child supplies propositions; randomize changes their order and limit restricts the number used. iterate consumes the next proposition, and has_more_items tests whether the iterator has values remaining.

For example, to visit at most two propositions in randomized order:

<iterator name="suggested_activity">
  <enumerate randomize="true" limit="2">
    <proposition predicate="activity" value="walk"/>
    <proposition predicate="activity" value="museum"/>
    <proposition predicate="activity" value="concert"/>
  </enumerate>
</iterator>

The iterator is exhausted after the configured values have been consumed. After exhaustion, another iteration begins at the start of the sequence. Use has_more_items in the current pass to exit or branch before that restart.

See Domain queries for predicate-based enumerations.

docs.title: Plans and postplans
docs.text:
A plan is an ordered sequence of plan items for a goal. Items are represented in XML in execution order.

<goal type="perform" action="book_room">
  <plan>
    <findout type="wh_question" predicate="room_date"/>
    <invoke_service_action name="BookRoom"/>
  </plan>
</goal>

A postplan is an ordered sequence associated with a goal and can be declared for either a perform or resolve goal. The schema accepts both forms. Runtime execution depends on how the goal is completed or downdated: for example, ordinary perform-goal downdating runs its postplan, while not every resolve-goal downdating path does. A postplan is therefore not guaranteed to run on every goal-removal path. Use it for follow-up bookkeeping, such as forgetting temporary information or moving to another goal. A jump from a completed goal's postplan does not restart that goal's source plan.

For example, a trip-price goal can collect its inputs in order, request the price, then clear the temporary result after the goal resolves:

<goal type="resolve" question_type="wh_question" predicate="price">
  <plan>
    <findout type="wh_question" predicate="means_of_transport"/>
    <findout type="wh_question" predicate="destination"/>
    <findout type="wh_question" predicate="departure_city"/>
    <findout type="wh_question" predicate="departure_day"/>
    <findout type="wh_question" predicate="seat_class"/>
    <invoke_service_query type="wh_question" predicate="price"/>
  </plan>
  <postplan><forget predicate="price"/></postplan>
</goal>

Plan items can also occur in the then/else branches of if and inside once. See the plan-item index.

docs.title: Domain queries
docs.text:
A top-level <query> defines an answer for a predicate. A query has one predicate and exactly one body form: implications, random selection, or enumeration.

<query predicate="greeting">
  <implication>
    <antecedent predicate="time_of_day" value="morning"/>
    <consequent predicate="greeting" value="good_morning"/>
  </implication>
  <implication>
    <antecedent predicate="time_of_day" value="evening"/>
    <consequent predicate="greeting" value="good_evening"/>
  </implication>
</query>
  • Implications: each antecedent may be one proposition or a configuration; all propositions in a configuration must hold. Define exhaustive cases for the expected state space.
  • Random selection: <select_at_random> contains individuals; consecutive calls may return the same individual.
  • Enumeration: <enumerate> returns individuals in declaration order and restarts after its final value. Set randomize="true" to randomize the order.

Choose a value at random; repeated calls may choose the same value:

<query predicate="direction">
  <select_at_random>
    <individual value="left"/>
    <individual value="right"/>
  </select_at_random>
</query>

Enumerate all declared values in sequence:

<query predicate="season_to_consider">
  <enumerate>
    <individual value="spring"/>
    <individual value="summer"/>
    <individual value="autumn"/>
    <individual value="winter"/>
  </enumerate>
</query>

To enumerate the same values in random order, set randomize="true" on enumerate. For implication bodies with multiple conditions, place all antecedent propositions inside one <antecedent>; every proposition must hold for that implication to match.

invoke_domain_query resolves a question through a matching domain query. Use reset_domain_query to restart an enumeration. has_more_items can test for remaining values.

docs.title: Question parameters
docs.text:
A <parameters> declaration configures how a particular question is handled. It is keyed by predicate, optionally qualified by question_type.

<parameters question_type="wh_question" predicate="person" source="service"
            incremental="true" max_reported_hit_count="10">
  <service_query type="wh_question" predicate="person"/>
  <ask_feature predicate="person_name"/>
  <ask_feature predicate="person_city" kpq="true"/>
</parameters>

Important attributes include:

Attribute Meaning source domain or service; selects where incremental-search results come from. incremental Enables incremental search. verbalize Controls whether the question is verbalized. allow_goal_accommodation Allows goal accommodation for the question. always_ground Controls grounding behavior. max_spoken_alts Maximum alternatives spoken; minimum 1. max_reported_hit_count Maximum hits reported; minimum 1. on_zero_hits_action Action run when search returns no hits. on_too_many_hits_action Action run when too many hits remain. sort_order Currently alphabetic.

Children can include service_query, ask_feature, alt, hint, proposition, resolve, perform, related_information, and always_relevant. With source="service", provide a service_query; ask features refine the search. background and graphical_type are not part of the XML schema.

For child element details, see Ask features, Hints, Service queries, always_relevant, and Alternative choices. The separate plan item invoke_service_query invokes a Service Interface query from a plan.

docs.title: Service queries in question parameters
docs.text:
<service_query> selects the question sent to a service during incremental search. It is a child of question parameters, not a standalone plan item; invoke_service_query is the plan item that invokes a service query during a plan.

<parameters question_type="wh_question" predicate="contact"
            source="service" incremental="true"
            max_spoken_alts="5" max_reported_hit_count="15">
  <service_query type="wh_question" predicate="available_contact"/>
  <ask_feature predicate="contact_name"/>
  <ask_feature predicate="contact_city" kpq="true"/>
</parameters>

With source="service" and incremental="true", the service query supplies the candidate results and each ask_feature narrows them. The child question uses the same question forms as other domain questions. See Question parameters and Ask features.

docs.title: Domain validators
docs.text:
A domain-level <validator> lists valid configurations of propositions. Each configuration is a conjunction; the declared configurations are alternatives.

<validator name="DestinationValidity">
  <configuration>
    <proposition predicate="destination" value="karlstad"/>
  </configuration>
  <configuration>
    <proposition predicate="destination" value="gothenburg"/>
  </configuration>
</validator>

name identifies the validator. The XML compiler reads configuration children; DDD JSON represents them as valid_configurations. The runtime checks whether supplied propositions are compatible with at least one declared configuration. A configuration can match partially: values for every predicate in the configuration are not required. If supplied values contradict every configuration, validation rejects them and identifies the validator in the rejection move. This declaration validates domain facts and differs from a Service Interface validator, which calls an external operation.

docs.title: assume_issue
docs.text:
Assumes that the user has asked a question, making the corresponding issue relevant without asking the user to state it. The DDD should contain a matching resolve goal for that question.

<assume_issue type="wh_question" predicate="departure_time"/>

docs.title: Attributes and children
Placement and related items
docs.text:
Can appear in a goal's plan or postplan, or in an if branch. It has no plan-item children other than question content. Unlike raise, it represents an issue as already asked by the user. Unlike findout, it does not itself ask the user to resolve the question.

DDD JSON form:

{"assume_issue": {"question": {"kpq": {"question": {"wh": {"predicate": "destination"}}}}}}

docs.title: assume_shared
docs.text:
Adds a proposition to the facts treated as shared between the user and system. It does not itself request an utterance.

<assume_shared>
  <proposition predicate="current_recipe" value="sourdough_starter"/>
</assume_shared>

docs.title: Attributes and child
docs.text: There are no attributes. The required child is one predicate proposition, whose predicate and value must match the ontology.

docs.title: Behavior and usage
docs.text: The assumed fact is available to questions and plan conditions as shared commitment. A matching findout can be considered answered with this value. Use assume_system_belief for private knowledge, or inform when the fact should also be communicated to the user.

docs.title: Placement
docs.text: Can appear in a goal plan or postplan, or in either branch of an if.

docs.title: assume_system_belief
docs.text:
Adds a proposition to the system's private beliefs. It does not add the fact to shared commitments or ask the user to confirm it.

<assume_system_belief>
  <proposition predicate="quantity" value="200"/>
</assume_system_belief>

docs.title: Attributes and child
docs.text: There are no attributes. The required child is one predicate proposition, whose predicate and value must be declared/valid in the ontology.

docs.title: Behavior and usage
docs.text:
The assumed fact is available to answer a question or supply a later service call, but remains private and does not update shared commitments. This does not invoke a service or a user-defined validator. Use assume_shared to set shared state, or inform to request a user-facing inform.

For example, a resolve goal can answer a quantity question from a known value:

<goal type="resolve" question_type="wh_question" predicate="quantity_of_water">
  <plan>
    <assume_system_belief>
      <proposition predicate="quantity_of_water" value="20"/>
    </assume_system_belief>
  </plan>
</goal>

docs.title: Placement
docs.text: Can appear in a goal plan or postplan, or in either branch of an if.

docs.title: change_ddd
docs.text:
Switches the session to another DDD.

<change_ddd name="navigation"/>

docs.title: Attributes and placement
docs.text:
Attribute Meaning name Required name of the DDD to load.

The element has no children. It can appear in a goal plan or postplan, or inside either branch of an if.

docs.title: Behavior and usage
docs.text:
The requested domain is loaded and the previous DDD-specific plan and goals are discarded. Pending, non-integrated moves may also be lost. Use this for a domain transition, not to jump between goals within one DDD; use jumpto for the latter.

<plan>
  <findout type="wh_question" predicate="destination"/>
  <change_ddd name="navigation"/>
</plan>

docs.title: end_turn
docs.text:
Explicitly hands the turn back to the user/client when this plan item is processed, even if the DME has more plan content.

<end_turn expected_passivity="1.0"/>

docs.title: Attribute and placement
forget_all
docs.text:
Clears the system's private beliefs and current shared commitments, then puts the top goal back on the goals stack. This is not a complete session reset or a history-erasure operation.

<forget_all/>

docs.title: Attributes, children, and placement
docs.text: There are no attributes or children. It can appear in a plan, postplan, or conditional branch.

docs.title: Behavior and usage
docs.text:
forget_all also clears pending non-integrated moves, hint indices, and iterators. It preserves previous commitments and does not clear utterance history, the question-under-discussion stack, or the agenda. The plan item itself is removed; it does not discard the remaining plan. Use forget or forget_shared for selective fact cleanup. Start a fresh session when a complete reset is required.

DDD JSON:

{"forget_all": {}}

docs.title: forget_shared
docs.text:
Removes shared commitments for a predicate or a particular proposition. Facts in private beliefs remain unchanged.

<forget_shared predicate="colour"/>
<forget_shared>
  <proposition predicate="means_of_transport" value="train"/>
</forget_shared>

docs.title: Attributes and children
docs.text:
Attribute Meaning predicate Optional predicate whose shared propositions should be forgotten.

With predicate and no child, all shared propositions for that predicate are forgotten. Alternatively, provide one proposition child to forget a particular value. Use one form at a time.

docs.title: Placement and examples
docs.text:
Can appear in a plan, postplan, or conditional branch. To clear all shared colour values while retaining any private beliefs about colour:

<forget_shared predicate="colour"/>

For a single value, use the child form above. Use forget to remove a fact from both private beliefs and shared commitments.

docs.title: forget
docs.text:
Makes the system forget either one proposition or all propositions of a predicate. The target is removed from private beliefs and shared commitments.

<forget predicate="colour"/>
<forget>
  <proposition predicate="means_of_transport" value="train"/>
</forget>

docs.title: Attributes and children
docs.text:
Attribute Meaning predicate Optional predicate whose propositions should be forgotten.

With predicate and no child, all propositions for that predicate are forgotten. Alternatively, provide one proposition child to forget a particular value. Use one form at a time.

docs.title: Placement and examples
docs.text:
Can appear in a plan, postplan, or conditional branch. To clear all colour values:

<forget predicate="colour"/>

Use forget_shared to remove a fact from shared commitments while leaving private beliefs unchanged. Use forget_all to clear private beliefs and current shared commitments and put the top goal back on the goals stack; it is not a complete session reset.

docs.title: get_done
docs.text:
Requests that the user perform an ontology action. The item completes when the user reports that the requested action is done.

<get_done action="add_water" step="1"/>

docs.title: Attributes and children
docs.text:
Attribute Meaning action Required ontology action requested from the user. step Optional integer step number.

The element has no children. Use the action request for a task the user carries out; invoke_service_action instead asks a service to perform an operation.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Request an action without a step number:

<get_done action="add_water"/>

When the action is part of a numbered procedure, include its step number:

<get_done action="add_water" step="1"/>

docs.title: greet
docs.text:
Requests a greeting move.

<greet/>

docs.title: Attributes, children, and placement
docs.text: The element has no attributes or children. It can appear in a plan, postplan, or conditional branch.

docs.title: Behavior and JSON
docs.text:
Requests a greet move from the runtime. Use this explicit plan item when a greeting is part of the dialogue flow.

{"greet": {}}

docs.title: if
docs.text:
Branches on the result of one condition expression. The element can be used recursively to express multi-step decisions.

<if>
  <has_shared_value predicate="sourdough_status"/>
  <then><jumpto type="perform" action="freshen_up_sourdough"/></then>
  <else><jumpto type="perform" action="start_sourdough"/></else>
</if>

docs.title: Children and placement
docs.text: The first child is exactly one condition expression. It may be a proposition, a value/store condition, an iterator/query availability test, or a Boolean composition. Optional then and else children each contain a plan. Either branch can contain plan items, including nested if items; an absent branch does nothing. The if itself can occur in a plan, postplan, or conditional branch.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Jump to a different perform goal depending on whether the DDD already has a shared value:

<if>
  <has_shared_value predicate="sourdough_status"/>
  <then><jumpto type="perform" action="freshen_up_sourdough"/></then>
  <else><jumpto type="perform" action="start_sourdough"/></else>
</if>

Assume a value only when the selected ingredient is water:

<if>
  <in_shared_commitments predicate="selected_ingredient" value="water_ingredient"/>
  <then>
    <assume_system_belief>
      <proposition predicate="quantity" value="200 g"/>
    </assume_system_belief>
  </then>
</if>

See Conditions for supported tests and their JSON form.

docs.title: inform
docs.text:
Makes one predicate proposition privately available and opens an issue so the system can communicate it to the user.

<inform insist="false" generate_end_turn="true" expected_passivity="2.0">
  <proposition predicate="first_name" value="Charlie"/>
</inform>

docs.title: Attributes and placement
docs.text:
Attribute Default Meaning insist false If false, suppresses the inform when a proposition for the same predicate is already shared. If true, informs despite an existing value. generate_end_turn false Adds an end-turn after the inform when true. expected_passivity 0.0 seconds Passivity duration used by the generated end-turn.

The item has one predicate-proposition child. It can appear in a plan, postplan, if branch, or a question-parameter hint. Goal propositions and other proposition forms are not supported.

docs.title: Behavior and usage
docs.text:
With insist="false", an already shared proposition for the same predicate suppresses the inform even if its value differs. With insist="true", the old values for that predicate are forgotten from both private beliefs and shared commitments before the new proposition is assumed and communicated. The inform does not itself immediately add the proposition to shared commitments. Keep multiple informs in one plan on different predicates: informs for the same predicate can interfere with one another.

Use assume_shared to update shared state without requesting an utterance. generate_end_turn="true" is equivalent to adding an end_turn with expected_passivity after the inform.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Inform a value:

<inform>
  <proposition predicate="first_name" value="Charlie"/>
</inform>

Inform and hand off the turn for three seconds:

<inform generate_end_turn="true" expected_passivity="3.0">
  <proposition predicate="first_name" value="Charlie"/>
</inform>

Omitting expected_passivity uses its 0.0 second default:

<inform generate_end_turn="true">
  <proposition predicate="first_name" value="Charlie"/>
</inform>

For a hint, place the inform in a question's parameters:

<parameters question_type="yn_question" predicate="added_water">
  <hint>
    <inform insist="true">
      <proposition predicate="helpful_information" value="added_water_hint"/>
    </inform>
  </hint>
</parameters>

docs.title: invoke_domain_query
docs.text:
Resolves a question using the matching top-level <query> in the active DDD.

<invoke_domain_query type="wh_question" predicate="greeting"/>

docs.title: Attributes, children, and placement
docs.text:
Attribute Meaning type Question type; defaults to wh_question. predicate Predicate for a predicate-backed question.

Question content follows the shared question syntax; the item has no plan-item-specific children. It can appear in a plan, postplan, or conditional branch.

docs.title: Behavior and usage
docs.text:
The DME sends the question to the currently active domain, which selects the matching top-level <query>. Both result bounds are set to one for this item. Use it for answers declared in the DDD; use invoke_service_query for an external operation.

<goal type="resolve" question_type="wh_question" predicate="price">
  <plan>
    <invoke_domain_query type="wh_question" predicate="price"/>
  </plan>
</goal>

An enumerating query restarts after its last item. Use has_more_items to detect exhaustion and reset_domain_query to explicitly restart its state. See Domain queries.

docs.title: invoke_service_query
docs.text:
Calls the Service Interface query associated with a question and makes its answer available to the dialogue.

<invoke_service_query type="wh_question" predicate="price"
                      min_results="1" max_results="2"/>

docs.title: Attributes and children
docs.text:
Attribute Default Meaning type wh_question Question type: goal, wh_question, kpq, alt_question, or yn_question. predicate — Required for a predicate-backed WH question. min_results 1 Minimum number of expected results. max_results 1 Maximum number of expected results; set above one to accept multiple results.

A yes/no question can use a proposition child; a KPQ uses embedded_question; an alternative question uses alt children. The item can appear in a plan, postplan, or conditional branch.

docs.title: Behavior and usage
docs.text: The service query returns an answer that becomes known to the system. If the question is a goal question and the answer is known, the system can provide the answer to the user. When max_results is greater than one, the service may return multiple results. Declare the queried ontology predicate with multiple_instances="true" if more than one fact for that predicate must be retained.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
WH query:

<invoke_service_query type="wh_question" predicate="price"/>

Allow two results:

<invoke_service_query type="wh_question" predicate="available_animal"
                      min_results="2" max_results="2"/>

Yes/no query:

<invoke_service_query type="yn_question">
  <proposition predicate="need_visa"/>
</invoke_service_query>

KPQ form:

<invoke_service_query type="kpq">
  <embedded_question type="wh_question" predicate="destination"/>
</invoke_service_query>

See Service Interface queries and Findout.

docs.title: iterate
docs.text:
Assumes the next proposition from a named domain iterator.

<iterate iterator="nice_destinations"/>

docs.title: Attribute and placement
docs.text:
Attribute Meaning iterator Required name of a top-level iterator.

The item has no children and can appear in a plan, postplan, or conditional branch.

docs.title: Behavior and usage
docs.text:
Each execution assumes one proposition from the iterator. Use <has_more_items iterator="nice_destinations"/> to test whether values remain; the condition is false when the enumeration has reached its end. A later iteration can begin again at the start of the enumeration.

<plan>
  <iterate iterator="nice_destinations"/>
  <if>
    <in_beliefs_or_commitments predicate="destination" value="paris"/>
    <then>
      <inform insist="true">
        <proposition predicate="info" value="we will see the Eiffel Tower"/>
      </inform>
    </then>
  </if>
  <if>
    <has_more_items iterator="nice_destinations"/>
    <else><signal_action_completion/></else>
  </if>
</plan>

See Iterators and Conditions.

docs.title: jumpto
docs.text:
Targets another goal in the current DDD.

<jumpto type="perform" action="freshen_up_sourdough"/>

docs.title: Attributes and placement
docs.text:
Attribute Meaning type Required goal type; use perform or resolve. action Ontology action for a perform-goal target. question_type, predicate Question descriptor for a resolve-goal target.

The element has no children. It can appear in a plan, postplan, or conditional branch.

docs.title: Behavior and usage
docs.text:
The target goal's plan is loaded and executed. After it completes, the original plan is reloaded and execution starts from the beginning of that plan. If the jump is not guarded, the original plan may reach the same jumpto again and loop. Guard it with once or if. That loop risk does not apply to a jump inside a completed resolve goal's postplan.

Run a target once:

<plan>
  <once><jumpto type="perform" action="freshen_up_sourdough"/></once>
</plan>

Choose between two goals:

<if>
  <has_shared_value predicate="sourdough_status"/>
  <then><jumpto type="perform" action="freshen_up_sourdough"/></then>
  <else><jumpto type="perform" action="start_sourdough"/></else>
</if>

DDD JSON uses a goal descriptor:

{"jumpto": {"goal": {"perform": {"action": "start_sourdough"}}}}

docs.title: log
docs.text:
Writes a diagnostic log entry; it does not produce a user-facing dialogue move.

<log message="About to invoke BookRoom" level="debug"/>

docs.title: Attributes and placement
docs.text:
Attribute Default Meaning message — Required diagnostic text. level debug Optional log level.

The item has no children. It can appear in a plan, postplan, or conditional branch.

docs.title: Behavior and usage
docs.text:
Writes a diagnostic entry when the plan item executes. It is for debugging and does not emit a user-facing move. Keep log text useful for identifying the dialogue step without including private user data.

<log message="About to invoke BookRoom" level="debug"/>

DDD JSON:

{"log": {"message": "About to invoke BookRoom", "level": "debug"}}

docs.title: once
docs.text:
Wraps a sequence of plan items that should run only once for its tracking marker.

<once id="initial_greeting">
  <greet/>
</once>

docs.title: Attribute, children, and placement
docs.text:
Attribute Meaning id Optional marker name. Reusing the same value shares once-state across blocks.

The child content is a plan sequence and may contain plan items including conditional branches. A once block can appear in a plan or postplan.

docs.title: Behavior and usage
docs.text:
Tala tracks the marker as a Boolean private belief. If it is already set, the block is skipped; otherwise Tala sets it and executes the child plan. The block can run again after a session restart or if its marker is forgotten with forget / forget_all. Without an id, Tala creates a unique marker. Nested blocks are compiled recursively. Avoid reusing the same explicit id for nested once blocks: they share the marker, so the inner block may be skipped after the outer block sets it.

An id lets separate plan and postplan blocks share one run marker:

<plan>
  <once id="initial_greeting">
    <inform><proposition predicate="welcome_message" value="welcome"/></inform>
  </once>
</plan>
<postplan>
  <once id="initial_greeting">
    <inform><proposition predicate="welcome_message" value="follow_up"/></inform>
  </once>
</postplan>

docs.title: raise
docs.text:
Raises a question/issue for the user without imposing the same answer-resolution requirement on the current plan as findout.

<raise type="wh_question" predicate="destination"/>

docs.title: Attributes and children
docs.text:
Attribute Meaning type Question type; defaults to wh_question. Supported forms are goal, wh_question, alt_question, yn_question, and kpq. predicate Predicate for a predicate-backed WH or yes/no question.

alt_question accepts repeated alt children. A KPQ contains one embedded_question. Other question forms can use proposition, perform, or resolve content as appropriate. The item can appear in a plan, postplan, or conditional branch. Unlike findout, it does not require an answer to continue; unlike bind, it explicitly asks the question. It is useful for optional parameters. allow_answer_from_pcom and alts_predicate are findout options, not raise attributes.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Ask which goal is relevant:

<raise type="goal"/>

Ask WH and yes/no questions:

<raise type="wh_question" predicate="colour"/>
<raise type="yn_question" predicate="side_order_fries"/>

Offer two questions as alternatives:

<raise type="alt_question">
  <alt><resolve type="wh_question" predicate="monthly_payment"/></alt>
  <alt><resolve type="wh_question" predicate="interest_rate"/></alt>
</raise>

Ask whether the user knows the answer to an embedded question:

<raise type="kpq">
  <embedded_question type="wh_question" predicate="destination"/>
</raise>

DDD JSON KPQ form:

{"raise": {"question": {"kpq": {"question": {"wh": {"predicate": "destination"}}}}}}

docs.title: reset_domain_query
docs.text:
Resets the enumeration state of a domain query so that its next invocation starts from the beginning.

<reset_domain_query type="wh_question" predicate="season_to_consider"/>

docs.title: Attributes and placement
docs.text: The question identifier uses the same type, predicate, and applicable question children as findout and a domain query. The item can appear in a plan, postplan, or conditional branch.

docs.title: Behavior and usage
docs.text:
Resets the enumeration state associated with the specified domain-query question. The next invoke_domain_query starts at the first enumerated value again.

<reset_domain_query type="wh_question" predicate="season_to_consider"/>
<invoke_domain_query type="wh_question" predicate="season_to_consider"/>

See Domain queries and Conditions for has_more_items.

docs.title: signal_action_completion
docs.text:
Signals successful completion of the containing perform goal and stops the remainder of the applicable plan.

<signal_action_completion postconfirm="false"/>

docs.title: Attributes and placement
docs.text:
Attribute Default Meaning postconfirm true When false, suppresses the success report move. action — Accepted by the XML compiler and stored in the model, but ignored by TDM.

The element has no children and can appear in a plan or conditional branch.

docs.title: Behavior and examples
docs.text:
The containing perform goal is treated as fulfilled. Remaining items in its plan do not execute. TDM completes the topmost system action; it does not use the optional action attribute. Omit action unless the target runtime has been verified to support it. By default, the runtime emits a success report of the form report(action_status(action, done)); set postconfirm="false" to suppress it.

<goal type="perform" action="make_reservation">
  <plan>
    <invoke_service_action name="MakeReservation"/>
    <signal_action_completion/>
  </plan>
</goal>

Suppress the report:

<signal_action_completion postconfirm="false"/>

docs.title: signal_action_failure
docs.text:
Marks an action as failed and stops or continues the containing plan depending on whether action is supplied.

<signal_action_failure reason="service_unavailable"/>

docs.title: Attributes and placement
docs.text:
Attribute Meaning reason Required result label used in the failure report; it is not an ontology declaration. action Optional ontology action to mark failed instead of the containing goal's action.

The element has no children and can appear in a plan or conditional branch.

docs.title: Behavior and examples
docs.text:
Without action, the containing perform goal is treated as failed, the remaining plan items stop, and the runtime emits a report of the form report(action_status(action, aborted(reason))). The reason is an identifier; it does not have to be declared in the ontology. With action, the runtime looks up the declared plan for that action and removes associated instructional goals. It reports the action as aborted only when the matching perform goal is active on the goals stack; otherwise, no abort report is queued. The containing plan can then continue. Use this form only when the named action has a declared plan and its perform goal is active.

Fail the containing goal:

<goal type="perform" action="call_someone">
  <plan><signal_action_failure reason="phone_not_available"/></plan>
</goal>

Fail an active action while allowing the containing goal to continue and complete:

<goal type="perform" action="cancel_calling">
  <plan>
    <signal_action_failure action="call_someone" reason="phone_not_available"/>
    <signal_action_completion/>
  </plan>
</goal>

The example shows the plan item syntax only; it does not create or activate the call_someone goal. The named-action form reports failure only when that action's matching perform goal is already active in the TDM goals stack.

docs.title: Actions
docs.text:
An ontology <action> names an action that can be the target of a perform goal or a plan item that refers to an action.

<action name="book_room"/>

name is required. An ontology action is a semantic goal name. A Service Interface operation name such as BookRoom is a separate declaration; connect the two in a goal and invoke_service_action.

docs.title: Individuals
docs.text:
An individual names a value of a declared sort.

<sort name="room_type"/>
<individual name="single" sort="room_type"/>
<individual name="double" sort="room_type"/>

Both name and sort are required. Explicitly declare custom sorts in the ontology; otherwise, the compiler adds an undeclared custom sort as static and issues a warning. Individuals are used as values in propositions and domain-query enumerations. Loading checks name syntax and sort membership; sort-specific normalization happens when semantic individuals are constructed from values. Dynamic sorts accept supplied values without this normalization.

docs.title: Predicates
docs.text:
A predicate names a property and declares the sort of its value.

<predicate name="selected_room" sort="room_type" multiple_instances="true"/>
<predicate name="room_capacity" sort="integer" feature_of="selected_room"/>
Attribute Meaning name Required predicate name. sort Required value sort. feature_of Optional parent predicate for a question feature. multiple_instances Allows multiple values when true.

Predicates are referenced by propositions, questions, conditions, and service parameters. Declare the sort explicitly; declaration order does not matter. A predicate with feature_of is used to ask about features of the parent predicate, including in incremental search. See Question parameters.

docs.title: Sorts
docs.text:
A sort defines the value type used by individuals and predicate arguments.

<sort name="room_type"/>
<sort name="album_name" dynamic="true"/>

name is required. dynamic="true" allows the runtime to introduce individuals of that sort that are not declared statically. XML Boolean values are lowercase true and false.

Built-in sorts include boolean, integer, real, datetime, string, person_name, image, webview, and domain. Explicitly declare custom sorts in the ontology; declaration order does not matter. An undeclared referenced custom sort is added as a static sort and produces a warning. See predicates and individuals.

docs.title: Service Interface actions
docs.text:
An <action> binds a DDD service-action invocation to an application-facing frontend action or an HTTP endpoint.

<action name="BookRoom">
  <parameters>
    <parameter predicate="room_date" format="value"/>
  </parameters>
  <failure_reasons><failure_reason name="unavailable"/></failure_reasons>
  <target><http endpoint="https://service.example/book-room"/></target>
</action>

The name is required and must match the name used by invoke_service_action. The format requires parameters, failure_reasons, and target children, even when a section is empty. Use <failure_reasons/> when no failures are declared. Frontend-targeted actions cannot declare named failure reasons; loading rejects them. HTTP actions may declare them. See Failure reasons.

See Parameters, Failure reasons, and Targets.

docs.title: Failure reasons
docs.text:
An action's <failure_reasons> declares named failures the target can return.

<failure_reasons>
  <failure_reason name="unavailable"/>
</failure_reasons>

Each failure_reason name should match the reason returned by the service. Frontend-targeted actions must declare an empty list; the compiler rejects named failure reasons on a frontend target. For HTTP actions, an empty <failure_reasons/> means no named failures are declared; it does not guarantee success or mean that the runtime rejects failure responses.

Failure reasons apply to Service Interface actions, not to the ontology or domain validator. See Actions.

docs.title: Service Interface parameters
docs.text:
The <parameters> section declares values passed to a target operation. Each <parameter> selects an ontology predicate.

<parameters>
  <parameter predicate="destination" format="value"/>
  <parameter predicate="selected_contact" format="grammar_entry" optional="true"/>
</parameters>
Attribute Meaning predicate Required ontology predicate whose value is passed. format Optional; value or grammar_entry. Selects the frontend argument representation. optional Optional Boolean indicating the argument may be absent.

HTTP targets receive both semantic value and language-form fields; format selects the argument representation for frontend actions. See Actions, Queries, and Targets.

docs.title: Service Interface queries
docs.text:
A Service Interface <query> invokes an external operation to resolve a domain question.

<query name="available_room">
  <parameters><parameter predicate="room_date"/></parameters>
  <target><http endpoint="https://service.example/find-rooms"/></target>
</query>

The query name must match the ontology predicate of the question sent to the service (for this example, declare an available_room predicate in the ontology). TDM uses that question predicate to find the Service Interface query and sends it as the HTTP operation name. A domain service_query mapping can select a different question, but does not define an independent operation-name alias. parameters and target children are required. Queries require an HTTP target; frontend targets are not supported. The corresponding domain plan item is invoke_service_query.

See Parameters and Targets.

docs.title: Service Interface targets
docs.text:
Every Service Interface operation has a <target> describing where the operation is handled.

<target><http endpoint="https://service.example/book-room"/></target>

Supported targets:

Target Supported operations Purpose <http endpoint="…"/> Actions, queries, validators Calls the configured HTTP endpoint. <frontend/> Actions Delegates the action to the application-facing side.

Queries and validators require HTTP targets. The schema contains an entity_recognizer declaration, but the Tala Service Interface model does not load it as a supported operation.

See Actions, Queries, and Validators.

docs.title: Service Interface validators
docs.text:
A Service Interface <validator> calls an external operation to check whether supplied parameter values are valid.

<validator name="CityValidity">
  <parameters><parameter predicate="destination" format="value"/></parameters>
  <target><http endpoint="https://service.example/city-validity"/></target>
</validator>

It requires parameters and target children and uses an HTTP target. This operation is distinct from a domain validator, which lists valid proposition configurations inside the DDD.

The target returns an is_valid Boolean. If it returns false, the runtime rejects the input and reports the validation failure. Include the parameter values needed by the service in the validator's parameters section.

See Parameters and Targets.
